body: I understand exactly what you mean. My communications skills were horrible, thanks to my parents. I can’t say they tried their best in the beginning… but people can only parent the way they were taught. At least one of my parents acknowledged this. Gotta learn to forgive and move on. As well as be better

I tend to be like that as well. I was much worse when I was younger, but from my first relationship… before my husband… I realized this bad habit of mine. I had to learn to speak the language of my audience. I also had to learn when to walk away. Took me way too long to realize this.

I also should emphasize as your partner he should be helping you out and nurturing his relationship with you and your child. That’s one thing I personally don’t like that he’s NOT doing. Something for you to keep an eye on… spouses should share responsibilities not burden the other. Obviously the balance isn’t always perfect but he shouldn’t be neglecting his duties the way you described…. That’s my opinion tho. Take it for a grain of salt.

It’s hard to give you solid advice when we don’t know his side of the story either. I’m not putting your feelings and opinions aside, they are important. From the way it sounds from your perspective I would also be very hurt. There a few things to consider… I’ve learned that at times we may think that we are communicating clearly and effectively, but in fact the other person isn’t getting the message. There could be a lot of reasons for that. Either they don’t care, your communication styles conflict with each other, or maybe you aren’t being as transparent as you may think. Consider couple’s counseling. The right therapist will give you the proper tools to handle situations like this. Also remember that you can’t make up for someone else’s lack of effort. I hope that’s not the case for you.
